content_html:
A mild dusty smell at the first seasonal startup can clear quickly, but a strong persistent odor, melting-plastic smell, or smoke calls for shutdown and inspection. Not every “burning smell” has the same urgency.

First-startup dust odor should be brief

After months off, dust on warm surfaces can smell for a short time. If the odor does not fade or smoke appears, stop using the system.

Melting plastic or insulation points to electrical trouble

An acrid odor near a motor, wiring, or panel is not normal. Shut down from a safe location and call for service; do not open energized panels.

A clogged filter can contribute to overheating

On forced-air systems, check an accessible compatible filter. If replacing it does not solve the problem or the unit trips a safety limit, it needs diagnosis.

Gas, smoke, or carbon monoxide are emergencies

If you smell gas, see smoke, or a carbon monoxide alarm sounds, leave and follow utility or emergency-service instructions. Do not restart the equipment to test it.
